questions.stem: Which layer of the leaf is the main site of photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: The palisade mesophyll layer is the main site of photosynthesis because its cells are packed with chloroplasts and positioned near the upper surface to receive maximum light.

questions.stem: What is the function of stomata?

options.text: To allow gas exchange - carbon dioxide in and oxygen out
To absorb water from the soil

questions.explanation: Stomata are tiny pores (mainly on the lower epidermis) that allow carbon dioxide to diffuse into the leaf for photosynthesis and oxygen to diffuse out. Water vapour also exits through stomata.

questions.stem: Which cells control the opening and closing of stomata?
questions.explanation: Guard cells are specialised cells that surround each stoma. They change shape to open the stoma when turgid and close it when flaccid, controlling gas exchange and water loss.

questions.stem: What is the function of the waxy cuticle on the leaf surface?

options.text: To reduce water loss from the leaf surface

questions.explanation: The waxy cuticle is a waterproof layer on the upper epidermis that reduces water loss by evaporation from the leaf surface, helping to conserve water.

questions.stem: Why does the spongy mesophyll have air spaces?

options.text: To allow gases to circulate and reach cells for gas exchange

questions.explanation: The air spaces in the spongy mesophyll layer allow carbon dioxide and oxygen to diffuse easily throughout the leaf, ensuring gases can reach all cells for photosynthesis and respiration.

questions.stem: Why are palisade cells elongated and arranged vertically?

options.text: To reduce the surface area of the leaf
To help the leaf float on water
To allow more cells to be packed together near the upper surface, maximising light absorption

questions.explanation: The elongated, tightly packed arrangement of palisade cells means more chloroplasts are positioned near the top of the leaf where light intensity is greatest, maximising photosynthesis.

questions.stem: What is the role of vascular bundles (veins) in the leaf?

options.text: To protect the leaf from herbivores
To transport water and minerals in, and sugars out of the leaf

questions.explanation: Vascular bundles contain xylem (which brings water and minerals to the leaf) and phloem (which transports the sugars produced by photosynthesis to other parts of the plant).
